newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Sembawang Corp signs oil storage MOU.
newsitem.headline: Sembawang Corp signs oil storage MOU.

text.p: Sembawang Corp said on Monday it had signed a memorandum of understanding with Indonesia's Salim Group and Japan's Tomen Corp to build an oil tank terminal costing up to Singapore $200 million.

M.S. Tan, head of the Sembawang Engineering and Construction Group (SEMBEC), announced the pact after the official opening of the Karimum Marine and Industrial Complex (KMIC) and PT. Karimun Sembawang Shipyard (PT KSS) on Karimun island, Indonesia.
SEMBEC is part of Singapore's Sembawang Corp.
Tan told reporters the Salim Group and Sembawang Corp would each hold 37.5 percent of the equity and Tomen Corp would take the remaining 25 percent.
The oil tank termimal would have a storage capacity of 4.5 million to 6 million barrels and would be used to store oil products, Tan said.
He said 40 hectres of land have been allocated for the project, which would cost between S$100 to S$200 million.

KMIC is an integrated industrial facility for marine and engineering activities developed by PT.Karimun Indojaya Corporation, a consortium comprising the Salim Group, Sembawang Corp and Singapore's JTC (Jurong Town Corporation) International.
PT KSS is a 65:35 percent joint venture between Sembawang Shipyard and the Salim Group.
